_readme: Colours that are correct as literals because they are correct on BOTH themes.
Read by scripts/check-literal-colours.mjs; see that file for the rules that
pass without an entry here (a full-viewport veil is black by canon, a
rgba(0,0,0,x) cast lands inside a surface-inverse island, a gold or incense
literal is an accent and an accent holds its hue).
Entries are matched by file plus the exact class, never by line number, so
moving code does not rot the list. An entry the code no longer contains
FAILS the check: this file is a record of live decisions, not an archive.
Three families are in here and nothing else should be. Paper: the score
canvas, the printable route and the annotation marks that sit on them —
print and paper have no dark mode. The Google raster: a second paper one
surface further out, since the map stays light under a dark panel until it
gets its own map ID. And a specular mark on an accent fill, which holds its
hue through the swap and so keeps whatever is written on it.

features/annotations/components/Annotati.reason: Paper-side. The mark on the stave, its lock badge and the pin sit on a page that is white in both themes — the same exception as the canvas under them. The file's CONTROLS (note composer, phrase chips, read-only popover) ride the ladder and carry no literal.

features/settings/components/AppTab.tsx.reason: The install QR needs a light quiet zone or a scanner cannot read it.

pages/auth/LegalPage.tsx.reason: `print:bg-white` — the one printable route in the panel. Paper leaves the ladder at the printer exactly as the score's canvas does.

shared/ui/composites/PdfViewer/PdfViewer.reason: The page canvas. A score is paper and dark mode does not print on black.

shared/ui/primitives/Badge.tsx.reason: The pulse sweep across an accent fill — a specular highlight on a hue that holds, not a surface.

shared/ui/primitives/Checkbox.tsx.reason: The tick on the gold fill. Theme-invariant, and known to read only 2.29 against that gold — a real contrast finding (spec §1.2) that dark mode neither causes nor fixes. If it is ever taken up, `surface-inverse` is the answer already in the palette.

features/logistics/components/MapPinShel.reason: Painted directly on Google's raster, which stays light in both themes. A ladder token here inverts the pin into a dark disc casting a pale halo over a map that never moved.

features/logistics/components/VenueMiniM.reason: The pin's contact shadow on the same light raster.

features/logistics/components/MapAtmosph.reason: The frame drawn ON the map tiles: an ink vignette and a white inner bevel that belong to the raster's own light, not to the panel's ground.
